A release contour binary is about 474 MB. On Windows the copy is the whole install folder, on macOS the whole .app, and one such copy exists per release that has a daemon running or about to start, until it is unused. Old copies are pruned automatically, never while a daemon runs from them.

A packaged Linux install (/usr/..., Flatpak /app/...) runs in place, which a package upgrade cannot disturb. contour daemon --in-place opts out of the copy; a package upgrade may then replace the binary under the running daemon. A hand-started foreground contour daemon on Windows also runs from the installed binary.

The two negotiate a protocol version when they connect: each states the range of versions it speaks, and they agree on the newest one both know. Every release speaks the protocols of at least the previous two releases, so a client from a newer release attaches to an older daemon — and an older client to a newer daemon — as long as the two are within that window. Features the older side does not know are simply not used on that connection.

When the daemon's release differs from the client's, the window shows a quiet chip at the bottom right, for instance daemon 0.8.1 is older than this client. Clicking it offers Restart daemon on the new version. The confirmation says what that costs: it ends every shell the daemon hosts, and a fresh one opens on the new daemon. A daemon that keeps its workspace brings your windows, tabs, directories and scrollback back, and the confirmation says so (see Surviving reboots). After the restart a new Contour window attaches to the new daemon, and this one closes. The chip is shown only for the local daemon: a remote one (--connect-tcp) is not yours to restart.

The restart stops the daemon for an upgrade, then starts one the same way a client would: through the registered service when there is one, on demand otherwise.

Outside the window, or against a daemon from Contour 0.7.0 or another release before version negotiation, the client is refused, and it tells you both sides' versions:

the daemon speaks protocol 3, from a release before version negotiation; this client speaks 4-4

A wrong token is reported as such instead (wrong token or insufficient rights): the refusal names the daemon's versions either way, so a probe learns nothing more from it. To move past a version refusal, stop the daemon and let it start again:

contour daemon stop
contour client                        # starts a matching daemon

Remember that this ends the sessions it was hosting. An auto-started daemon rarely has the problem, since it exits 10 seconds after its last session and client are gone.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text:
• contour client opens a window. There is no terminal-only client at present; if you need one, attach with tmux -C through the compatibility endpoint described above.
  • You get the scrollback the daemon still holds, and no more. Attaching replays a session's history, but the daemon keeps only history.limit lines of it per session — 1000 unless the profile it was started with says otherwise. Lines that scrolled past that are gone, and there is no way to ask for them back.
  • A session sitting on the alternate screen has no scrollback to show. Attach while vim, less or htop is running and you get that program's screen, which never has history of its own; the shell's scrollback appears when the program exits.
  • Shells end with the daemon (see Stopping a daemon); the workspace comes back without them (see Surviving reboots).
  • ssh attach needs key or agent authentication. Contour never answers an ssh prompt — a password, a key passphrase, a second factor or an unknown host key — so run ssh USER@HOST once in a terminal first (see Remote hosts).
  • Images are not recoverable through tmux-mode replay (see the note under tmux interoperability).

For the architecture behind all of this — the two protocols, the delta transport, the stable row identity in the grid — see the internals page.

docs.title: Quick terminal
docs.text:
A global hotkey slides a terminal down from the top of the screen, from whatever application you are in, and the same hotkey hides it again. It is full width and 40 % of the screen's height, on the screen the pointer is on, in the Minimal chrome density.

It is off until you give it a hotkey: open Settings › General › Quick Terminal, press Record and press the chord you want. A chord needs at least one of Control, Alt and Super, and cannot be one the macOS menu bar keeps (such as Command-Q). Delete in the field removes it.

docs.title: The setting
docs.text:
quick_terminal:
  hotkey: { mods: [Control], key: '`' }
  hide_on_focus_loss: true
Key Meaning hotkey The chord, spelled as an input mapping spells its chord. Unset by default. hide_on_focus_loss Hides the quick terminal when another window takes the focus. true by default; with false it stays until the hotkey is pressed again.

Changing the hotkey takes effect at once, without a restart.

docs.title: Per platform
docs.text:
• macOS: the window is a non-activating panel, so the application you came from stays frontmost and keeps its menu bar while you type into the quick terminal.
  • Windows: the hotkey is registered with the system. Another application that holds the chord makes the registration fail, and Contour says so.
  • Linux: the hotkey goes through the desktop's GlobalShortcuts portal, which may ask you to confirm it. A desktop without that portal has no global hotkeys. Under Wayland a window cannot place itself, so the quick terminal opens where the compositor puts it and fades in.

With Reduce Motion on, the quick terminal fades in and out instead of sliding. So does it where another screen is stacked above the one it opens on, since sliding in from above would show it on that screen. The quick terminal never keeps Contour running while it is hidden: closing the last ordinary window leaves the process running only while the quick terminal is on screen, and hiding it then quits. Closing its last tab ends it, and the next press opens a new one. In daemon mode it is a window of this machine alone: its terminals run here and the daemon never hosts, saves or restores them.

docs.title: 0.9.0 (unreleased)
docs.text: Contour is now daemon-first: a plain contour shows sessions a daemon hosts, starting it when none runs, so closing the window no longer ends your shells. Reopen Contour, or attach from another machine over ssh or TLS, and they are still there. Set

docs.title: Its window and Settings are redesigned to feel native on macOS, Windows 11 and Linux, with a Terminal style of their own, a command palette, command blocks, split panes with cards and a status line.
docs.text:
• Adds the Connect picker, a small window that asks where a window's sessions should live before any terminal window opens: this computer's daemon (with its state and session count), this window only, a saved host, or an ssh:// or tls:// address typed in its field. Type to filter, press Return to connect, Escape to cancel, Alt+1 to Alt+9 (⌘1 to ⌘9 on macOS) to connect to the row shown with that number; a connection that fails stays under its row, in the words Attach to Host uses, with Retry and Edit Host…. It starts on the last target used
  • Adds File › New Window to… (Ctrl+Shift+K, ⇧⌘K on macOS), the NewWindowTo action, which opens the picker as a sheet; contour connect [TARGET], where TARGET is daemon[:LABEL], local, a saved host's name or an ssh:// or tls:// address and no target shows the picker; and contour connect --list [--json]
  • Adds the connect_picker_on_start setting (Settings › General, and the picker's "Ask every time Contour starts"), which makes a launch without arguments, as a Dock, Spotlight or launcher start is, show the picker first
  • Adds a "Connect…" action to the Linux desktop entry and a "Contour — Connect…" launcher, a "New Window to…" entry and the saved hosts to the macOS Dock menu, and "Connect…" and the saved hosts to the Windows jump list, with a "Contour (Connect…)" Start menu shortcut
  • Panes have default shortcuts out of the box: Alt+Shift+Arrow moves the focus (Cmd+Option+Arrow on macOS), Ctrl+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+O split (Cmd+D and Cmd+Shift+D on macOS), and Cmd+Shift+Enter zooms a pane on macOS. A configuration written by an earlier release picks them up too
  • The command palette's and the Settings window's selected row keeps the desktop's highlight colour but takes white or black text, whichever reads better, where the desktop's own text would fall under 4.5:1 (KDE Breeze's blue under white)
  • On Windows 11 the tabs are the title bar, on Mica, with tabs that join the terminal below them; the Settings window's title bar is Mica too and follows the chrome's light or dark
  • Hovering the maximise button opens Windows 11's Snap Layouts
  • Windows caption buttons use the Segoe Fluent icons, and the Windows chrome uses Segoe UI Variable and the FluentWinUI3 controls
  • Contour follows Windows' animation, transparency-effects, contrast-theme and accent settings, live
  • On Windows 10, and with transparency effects off, the title bar is solid
  • Rounds the in-window menus on every platform to its own menu radius (10 px on Linux and macOS, up from 3), with row highlights rounded to match
  • Draws command blocks as a rail beside the output: neutral for success (✓ on hover), red with ✗ for a failure, the accent with ▸ while running, in a fixed strip after the line numbers and timestamps
  • Shows how a command went right of its prompt, only where those cells are blank, so an RPROMPT is never covered
  • Adds a ⋯ button and a native block menu (Copy Output, Copy Command, Rerun, Open in Pager, Collapse Output) whose header names the command and how it ended; the block tooltip is gone
  • Adds ⌘↑/⌘↓ to step through command blocks, ⇧⌘↑/⇧⌘↓ to select their output, and Ctrl+Enter or Shift+F10 to open a focused block's menu; VoiceOver says how each command went. Adds the FocusPreviousCommand, FocusNextCommand, SelectPreviousCommandOutput, SelectNextCommandOutput, OpenBlockMenu, ClearCommandBlockFocus and ToggleCommandFold actions and the BlockFocus input mode
  • Folded output reads "80 lines hidden ⌄"; the sticky command header moves into the pane header or the title band
  • Draws scrollbar ticks as solid for failures, hollow for running commands and yellow for search matches; scrollbar.marks gains running and search_matches
  • Moves keyboard focus into the tab bar and toolbar with Ctrl+F6 (Ctrl+Shift+F6 backwards), and on macOS to the toolbar with Ctrl+F5; in the tab bar the arrow keys move, Return activates, Backspace closes (asking first if a program may still be running) and Alt+Left or Alt+Right reorders, and a ring marks the focused item. A bare F6 still goes to the shell, and so does Ctrl+F6 when the window shows no tab bar or toolbar. Adds the actions FocusNextArea, FocusPreviousArea and FocusToolbar
  • Makes Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V clear the selection after copying or pasting under the built-in bindings, where it used to stay selected, as a generated configuration file already did
  • Offers to install shell integration for bash, zsh and fish when a shell writes no prompt marks: the card shows the one line it would add to the shell's rc file, and adds it only when asked
  • Shows and installs shell integration per shell in Settings › Shell Integration
  • Marks the history a restored pane brings back with a "Restored · session ended hh:mm" divider, ends a command that was still running at the snapshot as abandoned, and says once how many windows and tabs the daemon restored
  • Inserts the shell-escaped paths of files dropped on a pane, quoted for the program in the foreground and never run. A pane whose foreground program is not a known POSIX shell, PowerShell or cmd (every pane on Windows and every pane hosted by the daemon, and a multiplexer, ssh or another shell) refuses a dropped file name or link that holds a shell metacharacter, such as a quote, an apostrophe, a parenthesis, &, % or $, so a name like John's.txt is not typed there
  • Adds moving panes and tabs by drag and drop, anywhere a terminal can live: drag a pane by its header, or a tab, to the edge of a pane (a split), onto the middle of a pane (a swap of two panes), onto a tab, into a gap of a tab bar (a new tab there) or out of every window (a new window at the drop position). Hovering a tab for 600 ms opens it so the drag can go on into its panes, a ghost with a label (Pane → split left, Swap with htop) shows what a drop would do, a dashed placeholder marks the place a carried pane left, and Escape cancels. The shells keep running through every move, between windows of one process and, for daemon-hosted windows, between windows of different Contour processes; a window or tab a move empties closes without asking. A target that cannot take the pane (another Contour process without a shared daemon, a daemon too old, a tmux window) turns its ring amber and says why, and dropping there moves nothing. Adds the daemon's MoveNode and LayoutBatchEnd protocol messages behind the move-node and layout-batch capabilities; older daemons keep serving tab reorder, move and tear-off
  • Splits a pane when a tab is dropped on its outer edge, showing where the tab will go; a tab dropped in a pane's middle tears off into a new window as before
  • Shows the size indicator as a pill centred on each resized pane ("100 × 30", or "13 pt" while zooming the font), announced once to screen readers when it settles
  • Makes the scrollbar an overlay that follows the system's scroll bar setting and hides at the bottom of the scrollback unless a failed or running command or a mark lies above; adds scrollbar.mode (system, overlay, always)
  • Replaces the hyperlink tooltip with a target pill shown while the follow modifier is held, placed in the pane header or over blank cells and never on the prompt row; hyperlink_hover_tooltip now shows it on plain hover and is off in the new defaults
  • Draws hint-mode labels in the cursor colour under contour-dark and contour-light, dims everything else, and turns the labels to the selection colour once a prefix is typed; adds the hint_label_typed scheme key
  • Changes Settings to open in a window of its own, one per app, from Settings… in the Contour menu (⌘, on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+, elsewhere), the command palette or the OpenConfiguration binding. It opens with or without a terminal window, is brought forward when asked for again, and reopens where it was left
  • Removes the Settings tab from the tab strip and the Settings entry from the new-tab menu
  • Rebuilds the Settings window as General, Appearance, Keyboard, Shell Integration and Profiles, with a search field and an Edit contour.yml… entry; rows use switches, segmented controls, steppers, sliders, a font picker and color wells, in the look of each platform
  • Applies every Settings change at once and writes it to the profile's or the global side file within 300 ms, replacing the file whole; Revert Changes undoes the session's edits. A file changed in an editor meanwhile is never overwritten, and Settings shows that version instead. Profiles and color schemes defined in contour.yml stay read-only, with Duplicate to Edit
  • Adds a Hosts section to Settings, after Profiles: saved hosts are added, edited, renamed, duplicated and removed there and written to hosts/<name>.yml beside contour.yml, and appear under Attach to Host. A host's page shows the SSH or TLS fields its address calls for, says under a field what the loader would refuse in the loader's own words and saves nothing until it is fixed, and attaches a window to the host with Attach. Hosts defined in contour.yml stay read-only, with Duplicate to Edit
  • Shows a live terminal preview at the top of every profile page that follows each change before it is written
  • Turns the color scheme, link pattern and status line editors into pages of a profile, with a gallery of schemes, a contrast readout on every color well that says whether it reads, and renaming a scheme that moves the profiles drawing with it; the Status Line fields are on both the profile's page and the Status Line page
  • Adds Settings rows for the scrollbar's mark sources (failed, other, running and user-marked commands, and search matches), secure_input, input_method_editor_style and scrollbar.mode
  • Makes option_as_alt take off, left, right or both, so one Option key can type accents while the other acts as Alt; true and false are still read, as both and off
  • Reopens Settings on the page it was left on, and refuses a new profile or color scheme name a configuration folder could not carry to Windows, such as con or nul; an existing profiles/aux.yml or nul.yml still loads on Linux and can be edited and deleted
  • Adds macOS tabs as pills in a tab well within the title band, with a centred title while there is one tab
  • Adds one badge per tab for unseen output, finished commands and OSC 7501 program status, by priority: waiting, failed, working, done, new output. 'Working' and progress now use the accent colour
  • Changes the remote host label into a host chip that shows when the connection is reconnecting or lost
  • Moves the daemon version notice from over the terminal into the title bar
  • Reveals the tab bar in full screen when the pointer reaches the top edge, as a cross-fade under Reduce Motion
  • Shows the foreground process's name on a tab whose title is empty
  • Fixes the tab bar showing the window title where the indicator status line showed the tab name an application set with OSC 30: the new {TabName} placeholder shows that name, or the window title when none is set, and is the default tab_label. A configuration that sets tab_label: "{WindowTitle}" keeps the window title. This holds for sessions a daemon hosts too, and an empty OSC 30 now clears the name rather than blanking the tab (#2170)
  • Fixes contour daemon --label NAME and contour client --label NAME using the default daemon when run from a shell inside a daemon-hosted pane: the $CONTOUR_MUX the daemon exports no longer outranks a --label you give, as tmux's -L beats $TMUX. Without --label it still names the pane's own daemon
  • Fixes a background remote tab showing new output when it reconnects or resyncs; a program's own screen switch or clear in it still marks it
  • Adds a native macOS menu bar of six menus: Contour, Shell, Edit, View, Window and Help. The Window menu lists the open windows, and Help carries the system's search field
  • Adds native context menus on macOS: with the default ui_style: native, the terminal, title bar, tab and new-tab menus open as system menus; ui_style: terminal keeps the in-window menus
  • Adds a row of color swatches and Move Tab to New Window to the tab's context menu
  • Changes the in-window tab menu (on Linux and Windows, and under ui_style: terminal) to open below the tab instead of at the pointer
  • Adds the actions CloseOtherTabs, CloseTabsToRight, MoveTabToNewWindow, ShowAbout, MinimizeWindow and ZoomWindow
  • Changes key handling under the macOS menu bar: the terminal now receives every key chord except the menu's own (⌘Q, ⌘,, ⌘H, ⌥⌘H and ⌘M), including chords a menu item shows
  • Fixes a configuration with separate light and dark color schemes being saved as YAML that did not load back
  • Fixes the window background not following reverse screen mode (DECSCNM, as a visual bell uses), its restore by XTRESTORE, or a foreground color set while it is on (#2182)
  • Changes the notice shown while a window runs its shells itself, because the daemon could not be reached, into a banner that pushes the terminal down instead of covering its first line
  • Changes the window chrome under theme: terminal with a single color scheme to follow the focused terminal's background, including one a program sets with OSC 11
  • Adds Reduce Motion support on macOS: with it on, the cursor glide and the screen transition are skipped, and turning it off restores the configured durations
  • Shows a lock on the tab, in the pane header or in a pill over the pane while a program hides what you type, such as a password prompt, and turns on Secure Keyboard Entry on macOS for as long as that pane has focus; panes hosted by a daemon report it too. Adds secure_input (auto, off)
  • Adds a one-time offer of the new defaults to a configuration that states no defaults_edition, and after Reset Config; it is never shown for an explicit classic, a locked configuration or a settings.yml that does not parse
  • Changes the first-launch defaults, for a newly generated configuration only (defaults_edition: native2026): JetBrains Mono (Cascadia Mono on Windows) at 13 pt on macOS and 12 pt elsewhere, a 100×30 window with small margins, the contour-light and contour-dark color schemes following the system appearance, the indicator status line, the tab bar once there is a second tab, a silent bell, 10000 lines of scrollback, a steady block cursor and Command+click to follow links on macOS. An existing configuration without the key keeps every previous default
  • Changes the default theme to terminal: the window chrome turns light or dark with the default profile's background
  • Changes the focus frame to appear only in a split tab, where it tells the active pane apart, and to use the system highlight color
  • Changes a running command block's derived status color from yellow to blue, so it no longer reads as a search match
  • Adds the built-in color schemes contour-dark, contour-light and contour-classic, every text color of which stays readable on its background
  • Adds Command, Option, Shift and Control glyphs (⌘⌥⇧⌃) to shortcuts shown in the command palette and the settings page on macOS
  • Bundles the JetBrains Mono font (SIL Open Font License 1.1) on macOS and Linux, so the default font is present without installing it
  • Bundles the Nerd Fonts symbols font (MIT License) on every platform, so glyphs of Nerd Fonts, such as Powerline, Font Awesome, Material Design and Devicons, render with whichever font a profile chooses, after the fallbacks it lists and before the system's; CONTOUR_NERD_FONT_SYMBOLS selects at build time whether it is fetched, handed in as an archive, or left out
  • Keeps the input method's candidate window at the cursor cell, including at the end of a line and while panes move or the font changes, instead of the pane's corner
  • Draws text being composed by an input method inline, at the cursor, or to its left when it would not fit, in the terminal's default colours with a thin (one logical point) underline, in the new defaults; adds input_method_editor_style (inline, highlighted)
  • Fixes text being composed by an input method not being shown on a line of plain text, and running off the right edge of the line; at the end of a line it now moves left to stay in view
  • Names the command a daemon restart stopped in each restored pane, with Run Again (after asking) and Dismiss
  • Offers Reconnect in a pane that lost its daemon connection
  • Daemon: every window, tab and pane has a stable UUID, and each hosted shell finds its own with $CONTOUR_PANE, $CONTOUR_TAB, $CONTOUR_WINDOW and $CONTOUR_DAEMON.
  • Daemon: serves a typed control API on its native socket: list, capture and label windows, tabs and panes, open tabs and splits, type into panes, read and wait for command blocks, and subscribe to events.
  • Daemon: contour daemon --access-file FILE issues TCP tokens with narrower control API grants (read, screen, input, write); a call outside them is refused as forbidden, and a narrow token cannot attach.
  • Daemon: a new daemon: configuration section, and --daemon-mode per launch, choose where sessions are hosted: auto (the default) in a daemon with an in-process fallback and a notice when none can be reached, in_process in the window's own process, required in a daemon or not at all; socket, size_policy and history_limit configure the daemon itself.
  • Daemon: a plain contour now shows sessions that a daemon hosts, starting it when none runs, so closing the window no longer ends your shells; set daemon: { mode: in_process } or pass --daemon-mode in_process to keep them in the window as before.
  • Daemon: a window attached to a daemon survives a lost connection: its panes show "Reconnecting…" while it reconnects with backoff, a connection gone half-open is noticed by a heartbeat, input typed meanwhile is dropped rather than replayed, and a pane closed meanwhile is closed on the daemon once it answers.
  • Daemon: contour client --window N shows one daemon window; a tab's profile is resolved in the daemon's configuration, and its active pane, zoom, title and color reach every other attached client; a client smaller than the shared grid follows the cursor.
  • Daemon: picks up edits of its configuration file without a restart: new sessions use the edited profiles, and running ones take the new scrollback limits.
  • Extensions: a status-line extension that contour daemon hosts can call the control API: list, open, split, close and label windows, tabs and panes, type into panes, and read panes and command blocks. Its manifest declares what it needs (control read, screen, input or write), the permission prompt lists each, and the answer covers the extension's commands too; the WIT package terminal-extensions:control@0.1.0 in wit/control describes the calls. An older Contour attached to the daemon is not asked about such an extension, whose commands then stay ungranted until a current one answers
  • CLI: contour ls, new, split, send, pane capture, close, label and api list, describe and call script the daemon's windows, tabs and panes, with --json output and distinct exit statuses; contour block list and read, wait, and events read command blocks and follow events.
  • CLI: contour agent setup installs a generated skill that teaches Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents to operate Contour panes.
  • Adds OSC 7501 program status: a program reports that it is working, done, blocked on the user or failed, and each terminal keeps up to 64 such records, dropping working and blocked ones at the next prompt or when the process exits.
  • Daemon: mirrors each pane's OSC 7501 program status to attached clients, lists it in contour ls --json and emits pane.programStatusChanged events.
  • The tab strip shows a badge for a tab whose program is working, waiting for the user, done or failed (OSC 7501), with the program's message as its tooltip, invisible formatting characters removed.
  • DEC mode 2034's SBQUERY answers an older command block by its id (Ps 4), and its JSON, now version 2, gives each block its id, working directory, start time and duration; every version 1 field is unchanged.
  • Adds the status-line placeholders {Cwd}, {Git} (read from .git/HEAD, no process spawned), {LastCommand}, {Selection} and {Scroll}
  • Adds color roles to the status line: a color may name a scheme role (Color=accent|success|danger|warning|muted), so one template reads well in every scheme; hex colors still work
  • Adds Hide=<mode> and Chip to {InputMode}, and MaxWidth= to {Cwd} and {LastCommand}
  • Changes a status line too wide for its pane to drop its least important items first, right to left
  • Changes the new default status line to show where you are, the branch, how the last command went and the scroll position
  • Paints the macOS tab bar in a tint of the terminal background, solid also under Reduce Transparency and in full screen
  • Sizes the macOS tab bar from the window's own title bar, and places it below the menu bar in full screen
  • Grows the macOS tab bar under ui_style: terminal to whole rows around the window buttons
  • Requires Qt 6.9 or later for the GUI on macOS; configure rejects an older Qt there
  • Adds pane cards with headers once a tab is split: the program, its working directory, its status, and split, zoom and close buttons on hover. A single pane stays edge to edge
  • Shows the focused pane by dimming the others instead of an outline
  • Makes the gap between panes the divider, with a wider grab area and a grabber on hover
  • Adds chrome_density: comfortable | minimal; Minimal draws 1-pt split lines without headers (hold Option or Alt to show them over the panes) and, on macOS, a bare band in the terminal background for a single tab
  • Replaces the 'press any key' notice of a pane whose shell ended early, failed to start or lost the daemon with a footer offering Restart and Close; Return restarts the pane in place
  • Shows a reconnecting pane as dimmed with a 'Reconnecting to …' pill
  • Groups the command palette's rows (Pane, Tab, Window, Layouts, Blocks, Profiles, Hosts, Edit, View, Shell, Contour), most recently used first.
  • Collapses commands that take a name, such as Change Profile, Launch Layout, Attach to Host and Switch to Tab, into one row that opens their list; typing a name at the top still finds and runs it directly. Escape steps back.
  • Redraws the palette at 640 points with one-line rows and the selected command's description in a footer, and opens it with a short scale and fade, a fade only under Reduce Motion.
  • Adds regular-expression and whole-word search to the find bar, beside match case; an invalid pattern says so in the count
  • Counts search matches in steps, so a long scrollback or a heavy pattern no longer freezes the window, and the count fills in as it goes
  • Searches match across wrapped lines, wide characters and accented letters however they were composed
  • Paints search matches yellow in contour-dark and contour-light, the current one stronger
  • Places the find bar at the active pane's top right under its header, moving it out of the way of the current match; under ui_style: terminal it takes the pane header row
  • Adds ⌘F, ⌘G, ⇧⌘G and ⌘E (Use Selection for Find) on macOS; Find Next and Find Previous wrap and open the bar when nothing is being searched for. Adds the SearchSelection action
  • Asks every permission (font change, large paste, buffer capture, host status line, rerun) in one dialog that names the action, with a preview of a large paste and a checkbox to stop asking for the session; questions are asked one at a time.
  • Shows configuration reload errors in the window, with a button that opens the file, and confirms copies, refused pastes and saved layouts with a short notice that screen readers announce.
  • Asks extension and control consent in the same dialog, with the permissions that can type shown in bold.
  • Save Layout says what it saves, stays disabled for an empty name, and asks before replacing an existing layout.
  • Refuses a buffer capture in a daemon-hosted pane instead of leaving the program waiting for the reply.
  • Draws a Linux header bar on GNOME, KDE Plasma and other Linux desktops: the tabs inline as pills, a new-tab button leading (a secondary click on it opens the profiles), search and a main menu holding the six menu-bar menus trailing, and the window's top corners rounded while it is windowed under client-side decorations
  • Places the window buttons in the desktop's order and on its side, from GNOME's button layout, KWin's configuration or GTK's settings.ini, with close alone on the right where none is set
  • Follows the desktop's accent colour, light or dark style, high contrast and reduced animation through the XDG Settings portal, live as they change; without a portal Contour starts as before, with the default accent
  • Adds the ContourLinux control style, so the Settings window, menus and dialogs match the header bar; the Settings window draws its own header row with the desktop's close button
  • Adds window_control_style: linux, the round symbolic window buttons, which auto now means on Linux, KDE Plasma included; plasma keeps the Breeze-like buttons
  • Adds a quick terminal: a global hotkey, set in Settings › General and unbound by default, slides a terminal down from the top of the screen and hides it again, and hides it when it loses focus unless turned off; on macOS the app you came from stays in front. Adds quick_terminal (hotkey, hide_on_focus_loss)
  • Shows a bell badge on a tab whose program rang the bell while out of sight, until the tab is seen; the Dock icon, the Windows taskbar button and the Linux launcher count the tabs waiting for you (OSC 7501 blocked), so a question asked in a terminal is visible from another app
  • On macOS, a command that ran ten seconds or more in a pane you were not looking at raises a Notification Center notification when Contour runs from its app bundle; clicking it brings the pane forward with the command's block in view, and it chimes only while the bell sound is on
  • Fixes contour help for commands with subcommands such as contour daemon: their usage lines now wrap inside the terminal width, under the command's first option, instead of running past it or indenting a subcommand's options by hundreds of columns
  • Resizing with text reflow now respects a finite scrollback limit and releases excess history storage; infinite scrollback remains unlimited.

Contour 0.8.0 turns the shell's command history into something you can see and act on: command blocks with exit-status marks, output folding, a gutter with line numbers and timestamps, a sticky command header and finish notifications, driven by OSC 133 or, on recent systemd, by OSC 3008 context tracking with no setup at all. It detects URLs and file paths in terminal output and opens them with Ctrl+click, replaces the search prompt with a GUI-native find bar, and adds kitty graphics animation frames. Terminal output throughput is up several-fold, reflow and resize keep text and the cursor where they belong, and a broad round of fixes covers Windows, Flatpak, daemon mode, SSH and the settings page.

docs.title: Tabs, splits and layouts
docs.text:
• Adds tab_color to profiles, giving newly opened tabs a default color while preserving layout, application and user overrides (#2152)
  • Fixes closing a pane or tab keeping its session — terminal, scrollback and threads — in memory until Contour exited. A program that ignores the terminal's hangup signal is now ended 200 ms after its pane closes, as WezTerm does, and a tab no longer leaks the picture of itself it takes for the drag cursor when its window closes mid-grab

docs.title: Window and desktop integration
docs.text:
• Adds status-line extensions (experimental): sandboxed WebAssembly modules, configured per profile under extensions, that draw an {Extension:name} segment of the indicator status line, or the whole line with status_line.extension, and are told of the pane's working directory, title, foreground process, input mode, tabs, user variables, progress, focus and font. Each pane runs its own instances on worker threads with a time limit per call and a memory cap, so a slow or failing extension never holds up the terminal; a profile without extensions starts none of it (#398)
  • Adds the bundled extensions clock, git, sysload, agent-status and plasma (#398)
  • Adds the run_command permission for extensions (allow, deny or ask): an extension runs only the commands its manifest declares, and with ask only once you allowed them; answers are remembered in extension-grants.txt, and a daemon's in a grants file of its own (#398)
  • Adds status-line extensions to contour daemon sessions, which run them where the session lives and ask their questions in the attached client (#398)
  • Adds remember_window_position to restore the first window’s position and monitor at startup without saving its size (#2164).
  • Adds the global option snap_to_rows to align window heights to complete terminal rows, avoiding unused space below a bottom status line. Available in Settings and disabled by default (#2158).
  • Adds notification_close_timeout, for the one thing the notification portal cannot do: tell an application that its notification was dismissed. Where a close cannot be observed, Contour now assumes one after this long (10 seconds by default) and reports it back over OSC 99 marked untracked, so an application that asked for close events with c=1 is answered instead of waiting forever, and can still tell a guess from an observation. A notification that states its own lifetime with w= is answered on that instead, and 0 disables the assumption entirely
  • Extends OSC 9;4 progress indicators to the Windows taskbar, KDE Plasma launcher and macOS Dock, including while minimized, using combined progress from tabs and split panes.
  • Changes the indicator status line to span the window's whole width: its bar reaches the window's left and right edges past the gutter and the page margins beside it, but stays its own rows' height, and its text is laid out across the gutter's columns as well as the page's, so its middle sits in the bar's centre. The host-writable status line keeps the page's width (#2139)
  • Changes ending a shell within early_exit_threshold with a successful exit status — exit or Ctrl+D — to close the window as at any other time; the "Shell terminated too quickly" notice and its key press remain for a shell that fails, is killed, or whose exit status is unknown
  • Changes OSC 777 and OSC 9 notifications to show only while their pane is not the focused one, as foot and Windows Terminal do, and OSC 99's o=invisible to mean while the pane is off screen: it acted as o=unfocused
  • Fixes Windows font metrics after moving between monitors with different DPI scaling, maximized windows not filling the usable area, and resize handles remaining active while maximized or fullscreen (#2164).
  • Fixes the Windows custom window frame growing the window and leaving a gap below the status line at startup: the client size is now preserved when the frame is applied (#2132)
  • Fixes status-line {Command} items opening console windows on Windows and slowing down rendering: commands now run in the background at a configurable Interval= (default 10 seconds), with a 5-second timeout, and accept the {Command:<command>} shorthand (#2135)
  • Fixes clicking an OSC 99 notification that asks for focus only raising its window: it now brings its tab and pane forward, and so does clicking a tray message off Linux. Off Linux, a notification from a pane in a background tab was dropped. In a contour client tab an application's o=always or o=invisible was lost, and OSC 99's lists of pending and shown notifications grew without limit
  • Fixes desktop notifications never appearing in the Flatpak build. Contour asked org.freedesktop.Notifications for them directly, which a sandbox does not permit and which Flathub declines to grant a permission for; a sandboxed Contour now speaks the org.freedesktop.portal.Notification portal instead, which needs no permission at all. Outside a sandbox nothing changes — the session bus is still used, and still reports a dismissal exactly as before
  • Fixes the window freezing for up to 25 seconds when a hyperlink, folder or configuration file is opened while the desktop's xdg-desktop-portal is not answering. Qt reaches the portal with a blocking call on the GUI thread, and since Qt 6.10 it takes that path whether or not Contour is sandboxed; Contour now speaks the portal itself, asynchronously, and falls back to xdg-open if the portal refuses. Where opening still fails, the log now says why instead of only that it did (#2075)

docs.title: Command palette, settings and menus
docs.text:
• Adds a message to the settings page that says why it refused a value or could not save a change, which screen readers announce
  • Fixes a profile the settings page saves cutting a hint pattern's name short at " #", or no longer loading when the name holds ": "; and saving a color scheme that sets a context tint failing
  • Fixes the Rendering GPU setting never applying, while the settings page showed it as set, when settings.yml held a hand-edited renderer: value
  • Fixes the settings page's grapheme clustering and text scaling settings being saved but never applied
  • Fixes number fields on the settings page storing another number than the one shown or typed: in a locale that writes a decimal comma, leaving a field that showed 0.5, such as Background opacity, stored 5, and a whole number typed with the locale's thousands separator, such as 1,000, was stored as 1. A decimal field now takes a decimal point or a comma whatever the locale, and a whole-number field takes no thousands separator
  • Fixes a malformed entry in settings.yml or in a GUI-written profile being reported without the file's name
  • Fixes a settings.yml or a GUI-written profile file that holds a single word aborting the load of the whole configuration. Such a file is now skipped and reported, as one that does not parse already was
  • Fixes a settings field, switch or menu whose change was refused, or could not be saved, going on showing the refused value instead of the stored one
  • Fixes the settings page writing an override of a global setting's value already in effect, and offering a Reset for no change, when its field was left unchanged or its menu's shown entry was picked again. Escape in a field now puts the stored value back: it kept the typed text, which the next focus change saved
  • Fixes the settings page accepting, and saving, a PTY read buffer size of zero or less, a negative number of recent commands and a negative interface font size. It now refuses them and says why
  • Fixes the settings page's Keybindings list showing only the first action of a binding that runs several, and leaving out the built-in bindings that contour.yml leaves free, such as Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown switching tabs and right-click opening the context menu. They are now listed after the configured ones, marked built-in

docs.title: Hyperlinks, file paths and hint mode
docs.text:
• Adds detection of URLs, file paths (with their :line:column) and patterns of your own in terminal output: they are underlined like OSC 8 hyperlinks once output goes quiet and open with Ctrl+click, the context menu or vi's gx, and ]x / [x move between them. Detection runs off the parser and its file checks on a thread of their own
  • Adds link_detection to choose, per screen, whether URLs and file paths in output are detected; file paths are no longer detected on the alternate screen by default.
  • Adds hyperlink_decoration.mode (always, hover, modifier, never) and makes hyperlink_decoration.normal and .hover take effect, for OSC 8 and detected links alike
  • Adds file_opener, a command template with {path}, {line} and {column} for opening detected files, and clickable and url keys for hint_patterns; all of them are editable on the settings page
  • Changes hint mode's Open on a match of your own pattern whose text names no URL scheme to open nothing, as a link opens only a scheme Contour knows; give the pattern url: 'file://{0}' to open the absolute path it matches
  • Fixes hint mode freezing on long words, ending wide-character URLs early, misplacing highlights after combining characters and cutting parenthesised URLs short
  • Fixes a file:// link's tooltip and its click naming different files: the tooltip kept a #L10 fragment that the click dropped, and file://C:/dir was opened as the network path //c/dir
  • Fixes Ctrl+click and hint mode resolving a relative path against a working directory that another machine reported (file://otherhost/…), opening this machine's file of the same name; in a contour client pane mirroring another machine's daemon, Ctrl+click on a file path and file:// links opened this machine's file too
  • Fixes the status line's context breadcrumb and the hyperlink tooltip showing a right-to-left override or a control character a program sent as it was, which could reverse the rest of the status line or the link shown
  • Fixes a link staying underlined, with its tooltip up, after the pointer left the grid for the gutter or the window's edge
  • Fixes FollowHyperlink and OpenSelection launching what they open while holding the terminal's lock, so a slow launcher froze the terminal's output

docs.title: Scrolling, search and selection
docs.text:
• Adds search_case_sensitivity (smart, insensitive, sensitive), which the find bar's Aa button also cycles at runtime. Smart, the default, is case-insensitive until the term contains a capital, and it is Unicode-aware, so it works for non-Latin scripts (#1410)
  • Replaces the status-line search prompt with a GUI-native find bar floating over the pane: a real text field, a live match count, previous/next, and a case toggle. Opened by Ctrl+Shift+F, or by / in Vi normal mode; neither switches the Vi mode any more. Under ui_style: terminal the same bar is drawn as a TUI — square, cell-quantized, in the terminal's own font (#2081)
  • Changes the default auto_scroll_on_update from true to false, as in VTE, ghostty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal: a view scrolled back into the history stays there until you type. A configuration file that spells the option out keeps its value
  • Deprecates search_mode_switch, which chose the Vi mode to return to after a search. Entering a search no longer changes the mode, so there is nothing left for it to select; the key is still accepted so existing configurations keep loading
  • Changes {SearchPrompt} in the indicator status line to a read-only echo of the active search term, which no longer appears in the default status line
  • Fixes a view scrolled back into the history being brought down to the bottom about once a second with auto_scroll_on_update on, while a shell that redraws its prompt in place on a timer sat idle: only output that scrolls lines into the history now brings the view down, as in ghostty
  • Fixes search highlighting disagreeing with search matching for any non-ASCII term: the highlighter asked std::isupper, which is undefined above U+00FF, and asked it of the term's remaining suffix rather than the whole term, so "Foo" matched its tail case-insensitively
  • Fixes being unable to edit a restored search term, and pasting into the search prompt corrupting it — both consequences of the hand-rolled line editor the find bar replaces (#1353)
  • Fixes search and selection around double-width characters: a search missed a match running on past one, the highlight did not paint a match across one or across a soft wrap, and a double-click selected only part of a word holding one. A double-click also joined words across a hard line break, or took in the next word after a word wrapped onto a third row; vi's * and # had the same faults
  • Fixes a fast mouse click starting a drag selection from a stale position instead of where the button actually went down, making the selected region appear to jump the moment the drag started. A slow, deliberate drag never showed this, because the pointer's tracked position was refreshed by the preceding movement; a quick click could arrive with no such movement right before it
  • Fixes dragging out an ordinary text selection silently overwriting the active search term, so the selected text appeared as a live search wherever a status line or the find bar echoes it. Only a double or triple click's word selection is meant to do that

docs.title: Paste, buffer capture and permissions
docs.text:
• Fixes permissions.capture_buffer never being consulted: a profile saying deny still raised the dialog and let the capture through once approved, and one saying allow was still interrupted by it. Both now decide the request outright, and with ask, "Yes to all" / "No to all" is remembered for the rest of the session instead of being stored and ignored (#2089)
  • Fixes "Yes to all" on a larger-than-512-KB paste not being remembered either, so every such paste asked again
  • Fixes a refused buffer capture leaving the requesting program hanging. The reply always ends with an empty PM 314 chunk, and a refusal sent nothing at all — so a client reading until that marker waited forever. A denial now sends the terminator, and so does a capture asked of a background pane
  • Fixes a second buffer-capture request arriving before the first was answered being dropped, which left that request unanswered; requests are now queued and each one gets its own reply
  • Fixes a larger-than-512-KB paste bypassing the newline normalization every smaller paste gets, so a CRLF payload arrived with carriage returns that a shell reads as Enter — under bracketed paste that executed the pasted lines instead of inserting them. Such a paste also honours the repeat count and whitespace-stripping it was asked for, and is no longer re-read from the clipboard when approved, so what is pasted is what was measured and shown rather than whatever was copied while the dialog was up
  • Fixes pasted text ending a bracketed paste early with an embedded ESC [ 201 ~, or its 8-bit form, so that the rest reached the shell as typed keys: copying a command's output and pasting it back was enough to run what it held. ESC and C1 controls are now dropped inside a bracketed paste, and hint mode's Paste goes the same way

docs.title: Daemon mode and remote sessions
docs.text:
• Changes an SSH profile that cannot connect to say so on the terminal, naming the host, the port and the reason. Every such failure — a name that does not resolve, a refused connection, an agent that is not there — used to be written only to the error log, which is off by default, so what appeared was the generic "Shell terminated too quickly." with nothing in it to act on (#2075)
  • Changes an SSH profile under Flatpak that fails because the sandbox permits no network to say that, rather than reporting the host as unresolvable. Contour's SSH runs in-process rather than spawning ssh, so it is subject to the sandbox's own network permission; the message is chosen from what the sandbox reports it was granted, not guessed from how the call failed (#2075)
  • Fixes contour daemon and contour client silently ignoring a profile's shell, escape_sandbox and presentation (cursor, status line, scrolling, colors) settings, hosting every session with the bare OS login shell and default presentation instead — even on the very first daemon spawn, not only when an already-running daemon was reused (#2092)
  • Fixes contour daemon not realizing a profile's configured default_layout when it starts: it now does, so the first contour client to attach sees the real layout instead of always a single pane — including each pane's own command, arguments and directory, not just its tab/pane shape. A pane's per-tab profile override is not honored on the daemon and is logged.
  • Fixes contour daemon retrying forever, every 100 ms, once its listening socket was gone, serving nothing and saying only that an accept had failed. It now stops accepting there and logs why
  • Fixes ClearHistoryAndReset, SoftReset and WriteScreen in a tab attached to contour daemon acting only on the client's copy of the screen, which the next update could undo. They now run on the daemon
  • Fixes a daemon with more than one scrollback-heavy pane becoming permanently unattachable — contour client was refused before any screen content arrived, and every reconnect failed the same way. Attach snapshots are now paced against the connection's send queue and split across frames, so attaching succeeds whatever the scrollback depth; a window resize could drop an already-attached client for the same reason and no longer does
  • Fixes contour client never finding the daemon under Flatpak. A sandboxed daemon bound its socket under the sandbox's own $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR — a directory on a private mount the host cannot reach at any path — so a shell that escaped the sandbox had nothing to attach to. It now binds under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/, which flatpak shares with the host at the same path, and exports $CONTOUR_MUX into the shells it hosts (#2075)
  • Fixes an SSH connection attempt skipping every other address a host name resolved to, so a host reachable only at its second address appeared to be down
  • Fixes Contour hanging when an SSH handshake failed: the failure path took a lock the calling thread already held
  • Fixes Contour spinning when the SSH agent could not be reached — the normal case inside a Flatpak, where $SSH_AUTH_SOCK names a host path the sandbox does not mount — instead of falling through to the next authentication method

docs.title: Keyboard and mouse input
docs.text:
• Adds Ctrl+Shift+Up and Ctrl+Shift+Down to move between command prompts on the primary screen, as in Ghostty (ScrollMarkUp and ScrollMarkDown); a full-screen application keeps the chord
  • Fixes AltGr characters arriving on Windows as control codes: on a Swedish layout AltGr+8, 9, + and 2 typed ESC, GS, FS and NUL instead of [ ] and @. Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, and under the Win32 input mode ConPTY enables, the character was Ctrl-mapped as if Ctrl had been pressed. A Ctrl+Alt that produced a printable character is now treated as AltGr, while a genuine Ctrl+Alt chord is still reported as one (#2127)
  • Fixes a genuine Ctrl+Alt+key on Windows losing both modifiers outside the Win32 input mode — the case for SSH profiles: Ctrl+Alt+A typed a bare "A" instead of ESC ^A, or CSI 97;7u under the kitty keyboard protocol, and a key binding on a Ctrl+Alt chord never fired. Every Ctrl+Alt used to be taken for AltGr; only one that produced a printable character is now
  • Fixes a key binding for BACKSLASH firing on the x key
  • Fixes Vi mode on a page under 17 rows scrolling with every motion — j bounced the view, and H and L landed on the wrong edge — because the 8-row scroll margin was never capped. It is now capped as vim caps scrolloff
  • Fixes Vi mode's M landing one row above vim's middle row on a page of odd height, which could scroll the page by a row, and counting the blank rows that end a page collapsed folds leave short. It now lands where vim 9.1 does

docs.title: Rendering, fonts and Unicode
docs.text:
• Adds built-in drawing for more Powerline separators, including inverse dividers, thin chevrons and diagonal lines (#2160).
  • Adds U+25BC and U+25B6 to the built-in box-drawing renderer, so they no longer depend on the font
  • Adds renderer.gpu and a "Rendering GPU" settings entry to choose which GPU renders the terminal (Linux and Windows). The default, auto, leaves the choice to the system as before. Vulkan and Direct3D honour it with Qt 6.10 or newer; OpenGL honours it on Linux only
  • Changes the dotted underline to be drawn as evenly spaced round dots that continue across cells.
  • Fixes macOS configured font fallback, collection-face selection, and recovery of missing glyphs, including statusline symbols that require a proportional system fallback.
  • Fixes Windows ignoring the configured font fallback list and switching surrounding text to another font when a glyph was missing. DirectWrite now tries the configured fonts first and only replaces missing clusters. Also fixes undersized emoji and incorrect text/emoji presentation (#2140)
  • Fixes a combining character, such as an accent, that arrives in a separate read after a run of plain text attaching to the first character of that run instead of the last
  • Fixes a read that ends inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, right after a control sequence or at the start of the read, showing a replacement character in front of it and leaving the cursor one cell too far right
  • Fixes national flags after other text pairing their letters one off: a German and a US flag written after a space showed as D, EU and S
  • Fixes a cluster that starts with a combining mark or a zero-width character losing its first cell when the next character joins it
  • Fixes text in a script no installed font covers rendering at roughly 3 fps: every uncovered codepoint triggered a fontconfig sort of every installed font on the render thread, and every one of those sorts returned nothing. A single probe of the union of all installed charsets now answers the same question exactly, taking the median frame from 289 ms to 12.3 ms

docs.title: Images and graphics
docs.text:
• Adds kitty graphics animation frames (a=f) and frame selection (a=a), so applications can send only what changed between frames instead of re-sending the whole image. Self-running playback (s=2/s=3) and frame composition (a=c) are not supported yet (#2108)
  • Fixes images.sixel_scrolling: false being lost once a program reset the terminal (RIS), and never applying in a session hosted by contour daemon
  • Fixes the kitty graphics protocol's APC payload being parsed one byte at a time through the escape-sequence state machine, where the equivalent sixel payload has long had a bulk path. An image-heavy workload's time in the parser falls from 47% of its wall clock to 6.6% — 7.55 s to 1.06 s over 1.4 GB of payload

docs.title: Shell integration
docs.text:
• Adds OSC 133;N (as ;A), ;I (as ;B, for input that ends with its line) and ;L (a fresh line), the right-prompt mark ;P;k=r, and kitty's cmdline= form of the command line. A shell integration announcing commands with ;N used to get no command blocks at all, and under Nushell a command line ended in the right prompt's text (#1010)
  • Adds PowerShell shell integration: contour generate integration shell pwsh to FILE. Like VS Code's, it wraps PSReadLine's PSConsoleHostReadLine to report the command line (#1010)
  • Changes the bundled bash, zsh and fish integrations to report where the prompt ends (OSC 133;B) and the command line (cmdline_url), and tcsh to report the prompt end; with fish 4.0 or later, which marks its prompts itself (A, C and D from 4.0.0, the command line from 4.0.1, the prompt end from 4.3.0), the script adds only what fish leaves out (#1010)
  • Fixes a multi-line command split into one command block per line in Nushell 0.111 and later, which integrates natively and marks each continuation line with OSC 133;A;k=s: an A carrying k=s or k=c (a continuation prompt) or k=r (a right-hand prompt) is now read as part of the prompt in progress. Nushell never reports the command line, so Contour reads it off the screen (#1010)
  • Fixes a failed command being recorded and reported as a success when its OSC 133;D carried more parameters after the exit code, as WezTerm's 133;D;1;aid=42 does: everything after D; was read as the exit code
  • Fixes a command line sent as OSC 133;C;cmdline_url= being cut at a raw semicolon (kitty, too, reads it to the end of the sequence); and, with a shell that sends ;C but never ;D, the prompt after a command that printed nothing (cd, true) being taken for that command's output, so screen readers found no live prompt there
  • Fixes the tcsh shell integration on macOS printing its prompt and command marks as literal text such as \033]133;A\033\ rather than sending them: macOS's tcsh echo expands no escapes (echo_style bsd), so the terminal saw no prompts or command blocks there
  • Fixes the bundled bash, zsh, fish and tcsh integrations sending the working directory (OSC 7) as a raw path: a directory whose name held an escape character could send the terminal sequences of its own, such as a new window title, and a script sourced over ssh claimed a local directory. They now send a file:// URL with the host name and a percent-encoded path, and fish 4.0 and later, which sends its own, no longer gets a second one
  • Fixes the path of an OSC 7 file:// URL being taken as written: a directory a shell announced percent-encoded, as VTE's script, fish 4 and WezTerm do, showed as /tmp/a%20b in the tab title and hint mode, and on Windows a new tab could not open in it. A new window opened in the current directory also lost the part of its path after a # or ?
  • Fixes the bash integration installing no hooks when another copy of bash-preexec had been loaded first, as atuin and starship load it, and its hooks being replaced by a user's own functions named precmd or preexec
  • Fixes DEC mode 2034 semantic block queries reporting a command with another command's prompt and output, or at a fresh prompt the previous command's; a shell that enables the mode from its prompt hook never seeing the command typed at that prompt; a full reset (RIS) leaving the reader's session running; and a query of an unknown type being answered as one for the last blocks

docs.title: Command blocks, folding and the gutter
docs.text:
• Adds output folding: collapse a finished command's output down to its prompt line and expand it again. Driven by the shell's OSC 133 marks, so any shell with shell integration works (#88)
  • Adds a fold column in a one-column gutter left of the grid, marking each foldable block and highlighting under the pointer; clicking it, or the new context-menu entry, toggles that fold
  • Reserves U+10F000..U+10F0FF for Contour's own glyphs and assigns the fold column's two heads, which no Unicode character describes; see docs/vt-extensions/private-use-glyphs.md
  • Adds the global folding config section and the actions CollapseAllFolds, CollapseLastFold, ExpandAllFolds, ToggleFold and ToggleLastFold
  • Adds a record of every command block — its command line, exit status, start time, duration and working directory — kept for the last command_blocks.max_records commands (1000 by default), even after their output has left the history (#1010)
  • Adds exit-status coloring to the gutter's block column: a failed command's marks turn red and a running one's yellow (color scheme block_status), a running command shows ▸ and a finished one with no output ●, and hovering the column shows the exit code, duration, start time, directory and command line (#1010)
  • Adds line numbers to the gutter, off by default: gutter.line_numbers absolute, relative or hybrid, as vim's nu and rnu. Relative distances count the lines you see, so with a block collapsed 12k still lands on the line labeled 12 (#1010)
  • Adds per-line timestamps to the gutter (gutter.timestamps, gutter.timestamp_format): the time output first reached each line, at no memory cost per line (#1010)
  • Adds a "⋯ 1,234 lines" label after a collapsed fold, and vim's fold keys za, zo, zc, zM and zR in Vi normal mode (#1010)
  • Adds command marks on the scrollbar — failures, every command, and user marks (scrollbar.marks) — where clicking one scrolls to that command (#1010)
  • Adds a sticky command header: scrolled back into a long output, the command that produced it stays pinned above it with its exit status and duration (sticky_header.mode), and once that command's own line has been evicted from the history it names the command instead, so the header never just disappears (sticky_header.show_evicted) (#1010)
  • Adds actions on a command's output: Ctrl+triple-click selects it (SelectCommandBlock), CopyCommandBlock and CopyCommandLine copy its output or its command line (the latter safe to paste), Ctrl+Shift+G opens the last one in a pager (OpenCommandOutput, command_blocks.pager), ClearToPrompt clears everything above the current prompt, and CopySelection can fall back to the last command's output. Relative file paths in a command's output now open relative to the directory that command ran in. Ctrl+triple-click and Ctrl+Shift+G are built-in fallbacks, so they work even with a contour.yml that has its own input_mapping (#1010)
  • Adds desktop notifications when a long command finishes where you cannot see it, on by default for commands of 10 seconds or more in an unfocused pane (notify_on_command_finish) (#1010)
  • Adds command blocks to contour client sessions attached to a daemon: the gutter, folds, scrollbar marks, sticky header and finish notifications work there too, and reattaching never replays notifications for commands that finished while detached. OpenCommandOutput opens no pane there; bind it with placement: detached to pipe the output into a program (#1010)
  • Adds the gutter, command-block and folding settings to the settings page. Each one overrides a single key of its section in settings.yml, and leaves the rest as contour.yml says (#1010)
  • Adds a Command blocks group to a profile's page in the settings: scrollbar mark sources, the sticky command header and its evicted-command naming, and when, how and for which commands a finished command notifies (#1010)
  • Adds the block-status colors (success, failure, running), the gutter-text color and the sticky-header colors to the color-scheme editor. An unedited slot keeps following the colors it is derived from and says so, and an edited one can be set to follow them again (#1010)
  • Adds a menu for each command in the gutter: a click on a command's status mark, or a right-click anywhere beside its output, opens the context menu for that command, which can now also run it again (RerunCommand, shown and confirmed first) (#1010)
  • Adds gutter.block_column_width, 2 by default: the fold controls and command marks are drawn across two cells at twice the size, and a click anywhere in the column lands. A failed command shows a cross, or its fold drawn heavy; the fold under the pointer is drawn bolder (gutter.bold_on_hover) in colours a scheme can set per outcome (block_status_hover), editable on the settings page; and a click on a collapsed fold's "⋯ N lines" label expands it (#1010)
  • Adds "Copy Last Command" to the terminal's context menu, copying the last finished command's command line without the prompt in front of it; "Copy Last Prompt" copies the prompt's lines, PS1 included
  • Adds the profile option copy_command_preserve_multiline to preserve line breaks and tabs when using Copy Command. Disabled by default.
  • Adds history.hard_limit, which makes the scrollback evict a whole command at a time. Anything above history.limit is headroom the buffer may grow into; when it fills, entire (prompt, output) blocks are dropped from the top instead of a slice taken wherever the limit happened to fall, so the oldest line kept is a prompt with its command's output intact rather than an orphaned tail. Boundaries come from the shell's OSC 133 marks, so with no shell integration — or for a single command whose output is larger than the whole headroom — the buffer simply bounds at hard_limit and evicts line by line as before. Defaults to history.limit, which is exactly today's behaviour (#836)
  • Changes Vi normal mode to move in visible lines, stepping over collapsed blocks; folding.on_jump_into_fold picks whether a search hit inside one expands it or is skipped
  • Changes Vi normal mode's mm to set a user mark rather than a prompt mark: it is drawn as ◆ in the gutter and as a tick on the scrollbar, and no longer counts as a command boundary for folding or for history.hard_limit's eviction of whole commands, while [m, ]m and the im/am text objects still visit both kinds (#1010)
  • Changes the default scrollbar.position from Hidden to Right, so the command marks on the scrollbar are visible from the start. The scrollbar floats over the terminal's edge without taking a column, appears only while there is history to scroll through, and hides on the alternate screen unless hide_in_alt_screen is turned off. The new default applies to new configurations: a contour.yml written by an earlier version keeps scrollbar.position: Hidden, because Contour writes out the full default configuration on first run, so set position: Right in the profile's scrollbar section, or pick right for "Scrollbar position" on the settings page, to see the marks (#1010)
  • Fixes stale fold ranges after a command finished: OSC 133's ;B and ;D wrote their line flag without invalidating the ranges derived from it, so anything reading them between the end of a command and the next prompt saw the state from before
  • Fixes CopyLastCommandOutput on output of only blank lines putting a bare newline on the clipboard

docs.title: Context tracking (OSC 3008)
docs.text:
• Adds support for OSC 3008, systemd's hierarchical context signalling (UAPI.15): the nested stack of contexts a shell, run0, ssh or a container runtime opens around whatever runs inside it. systemd 258 and later emit these around every interactive command with no configuration at all, so on such a system Contour learns command boundaries, exit statuses and working directories for free (#2078)
  • Adds the {Context} indicator status-line placeholder: a breadcrumb of the contexts above the one you are typing in. It shows only privilege and machine boundaries by default and draws nothing at all when there are none, so an ordinary shell session is unchanged
  • Adds an optional tint map to color schemes, giving the page background a different shade under an elevated, containerised, virtualised or remote context. No shipped scheme sets one, deliberately: every field OSC 3008 carries is a display hint any program on the terminal can write, so the colour is something you opt into rather than something that appears
  • Adds fold controls, mark-jump stops and "copy last command output" to prompts without any setup on a system where OSC 3008 arrives and no shell integration is installed. A shell integration, if one is installed, keeps full ownership of the markers and nothing changes
  • Adds reporting of how a command really ended: OSC 3008 distinguishes a crash from an interruption from a plain non-zero exit, and names the signal — which OSC 133's numeric exit code cannot express
  • Changes the tab tooltip and "Open Current Folder" to follow the working directory OSC 3008 reports. A directory belonging to a container, a VM or another machine is never opened locally — the menu entry greys out rather than opening the host's directory of the same name. Set osc_context.enabled to false to opt out of all of it
  • Adds the same context tracking, tinting and breadcrumb to a contour attach pane that a local one gets

docs.title: New VT sequences and protocols
docs.text:
• Removes the deprecated SETMARK sequence (CSI > M); use OSC 133 ; A instead
  • Adds DECSR (Secure Reset, CSI Pr + p), the VT420 sequence that returns the terminal to its power-up state as RIS does, at every conformance level; given a Pr from 0 to 16383, Contour confirms the reset with DECSRC (CSI Pr * q) echoing it back (#2133)
  • Adds DECSWBV (CSI Ps SP t), the VT520 sequence for setting the warning-bell volume: Ps 1 silences the bell, 2 to 4 halves it, 0, an omitted Ps or 5 to 8 keeps it at the profile's configured volume. An application can only mute or halve that volume, never raise it, and RIS restores the default (#732)
  • Adds DECSMBV (CSI Ps SP u), the VT520 sequence for setting the margin-bell volume: Ps 0, 1 or an omitted Ps silences it (the default, per the VT510 manual), 2 to 4 halves it, 5 to 8 sets it to high, and RIS restores the default. Contour does not yet ring the margin bell itself — DEC private mode 44 remains unimplemented — so for now this only stores the value for when it does (#733)

docs.title: VT conformance and correctness fixes
docs.text:
• Fixes a single shift (SS2 or SS3) being used up before a character that the shifted-in soft font (DRCS) has no glyph for, which then came out of the wrong character set
  • Fixes resizing the window at a shell prompt leaving doubled fragments of the prompt on screen (narrower) or erasing the output line above it (wider): Contour reflowed the prompt the shell was about to redraw. The live prompt's rows are now cut or padded instead, as kitty does, and a prompt sent with OSC 133;A;redraw=0 is reflowed as before
  • Fixes narrowing the window leaving the cursor where its text used to be, so input typed at a prompt afterwards landed past the prompt's end or over its last character. The cursor, and the cursor DECSC saved, now keep their place in their line across a reflow, as in foot, kitty and WezTerm
  • Fixes a reflow changing the text it moves: blanks inside a wrapped line were dropped, a double-width character could be split across two rows, a block of OSC 66 text taller than one row was torn apart, and a line written with text reflow off (DECRST 2028) was reflowed anyway
  • Fixes a double-width character arriving in the last column being written with half of it off the page, after which a widening dropped the character that followed it (ABCDEFGHI中X read back without the X). It now moves to the next row, as in xterm, foot and kitty
  • Fixes a resize that changes only the height dropping a pending wrap, so the next character overwrote the last cell of the row; and a narrowing pushing a prompt on the top row of an otherwise empty page into the history as soon as it wrapped
  • Fixes a full-page scroll down (SD, or a reverse index on the top row) erasing the newest lines of the scrollback and moving the lines pushed off the bottom into its oldest slots. The scrollback now stays as it was, as in xterm, Windows Terminal, kitty and WezTerm
  • Fixes ED keeping a double-width or double-height cursor row at its size after erasing all of it, where DEC STD 070 resets it to single size; and EL 0 and ED 1 keeping two rows joined after erasing what joined them, so the next reflow or copy ran two unrelated lines together
  • Fixes clearing the scrollback (ED 3) leaving the view scrolled to, or the vi cursor on, rows that no longer exist, and a hint session open over the history matching them
  • Fixes writing to the host-writable status line after a narrowing resize writing past the end of its row, out of bounds in release builds
  • Fixes a DEC macro that invokes itself hanging the terminal, and a macro body larger than the free input buffer overflowing it
  • Fixes DEC macros (DECDMAC, DECINVM) to follow DEC STD 070: a macro runs where it is invoked, as if its bytes had come from the host, rather than after the rest of the output; the definitions share 6 KiB of macro space, whose room left DECMSR now reports (it said 0), and DECCKSR reports their checksum (it said 0000); a definition with a parameter out of range or a body that is not hex, or one made inside a running macro, is ignored whole; a body keeps no control characters; and the hex repeat sequence ! Pn ; … ; is understood
  • Fixes a full reset (RIS) keeping the macros, the user-defined keys and the soft character set while a soft reset (DECSTR) cleared them, the wrong way round by DEC STD 070, the VT520 manual, xterm and Windows Terminal. A RIS inside a running macro now ends it, and DECMSR and DECCKSR are answered from VT420 on only, as in xterm
  • Fixes VT screenshots (ScreenshotVT): a wide character replayed one column too far right, the line break after the last row scrolled the first row away on replay, OSC 66 text came back at ordinary size, and screenshot.vt drew from wherever the replaying terminal's cursor stood, in its colors and modes. The file now starts from a reset, cleared page
  • Fixes XTGETTCAP replies spelling a byte past ASCII, such as an 8-bit CSI, as FFFFFF9B instead of 9B
  • Fixes narrowing the window moving the cursor to the right: each column step doubled its column until it was pinned at the right edge, where anything printed before the application next moved it landed. Released versions showed this only with reflow_on_resize off

docs.title: Stability, performance and startup
docs.text:
• Improves terminal output throughput, fed from memory: plain text 166.6 → 310.9 MiB/s, coloured text 42.7 → 281.9 MiB/s, full-screen applications on the alternate screen 55.6 → 593.2 MiB/s. Lines with mixed colours and the alternate screen now take the bulk-text path, plain-text stretches inside non-ASCII text are written in bulk too, scrollback lines that scroll out are reused instead of reallocated, escape-sequence parameters are scanned in bulk, and each sequence is looked up through an index instead of a binary search
  • Improves reading from the terminal's PTY: the parser keeps reading while a frame is being built instead of waiting for it, and a burst of output schedules one redraw instead of one per read; plain text through a real PTY 69.8 → 104.2 MiB/s
  • Changes the default read_buffer_size from 16384 to 65536 bytes: the most read from the PTY and parsed in one go. Hosts that start sessions without a configuration file, such as contour daemon, move from 4096 to 65536 bytes
  • Fixes Contour not exiting for up to a minute or more after its window closed on systems where opening a GPU device hangs (seen with nouveau): loading Qt Multimedia for the bell no longer probes the GPUs for hardware video decoding and encoding
  • Fixes Vi mode's commands and mode switches changing the terminal from the GUI thread without its lock, racing with a program's output (a mode switch resized the page in the middle of it); a light/dark switch re-seeded the palette the same way
  • Fixes Contour hanging while local echo was on (SRM reset): SendChars hung on every use, and with in-band resize reports (mode 2048) on as well, so did toggling the status line, the key maps or input protection, changing the font size or resizing the window, entering Vi normal mode and switching back to the tab. Each sent input while it held the terminal's lock, and the local echo of that input takes the lock again
  • Fixes a reply that Contour raised from the GUI rather than from a program's output waiting for the next key press or output before it was sent, so a program blocked reading it could wait forever: the answer to an OSC 99 notification being closed or clicked, and the selection report of DECSET 2030 for SelectAll, CreateSelection or a drag that scrolls the view
  • Fixes a function key from F6 to F20 occasionally crashing Contour while a program redefined the user-defined keys (DECUDK) or reset the terminal: the key read the table as output rewrote it. Typing and the key-binding lookup also read the keyboard lock (KAM), local echo (SRM), auto-repeat and the modes a binding matches on, such as application cursor keys, while output could change them
  • Fixes an out-of-memory kill of any process running inside Contour, such as a compiler or a language server, closing Contour and every tab with it on desktops that start applications as systemd units. Each session now runs in a systemd scope of its own, so only the killed process ends. Building on Linux needs libsystemd unless configured with CONTOUR_WITH_SYSTEMD=OFF
  • Fixes closing a terminal whose shell could not be started, which made Contour wait for any other process it had started to exit and, on builds with standard library assertions enabled, abort. A process that was never spawned held the id 0, which POSIX reads as the caller's whole process group
  • Fixes a key press occasionally crashing the terminal, and a reply to the application occasionally losing its first bytes, which Neovim hit at startup: its DA1 query came back as just "2;314c" and was read as typed keys. Input flushes from the parser thread and the GUI thread could overlap, and each discarded the bytes both had written, so the next reply started that many bytes late; a key press shorter than that crashed. Flushes are now serialized
  • Fixes a crash (debug builds) or out-of-bounds memory access (release builds) when long or wrapping output reached past the 80th column right after startup: startup widens the page before it makes it taller, and the lines the taller page took over from the unused scrollback kept their old, narrower width. Every line entering the page is now resized to the page width
  • Fixes an application that opens a DECSET 2026 synchronized update and then stalls or dies before closing it freezing the display — not a slow frame, no frames at all. Rendering now resumes once a block has outlived 150 ms, with the mode register untouched so DECRQM still reports what the application set; on notcurses-demo the frame rate more than doubles, from 13.6 to 29.7 fps
